name: Whisper
what: Transcribes and translates interviews, video and audio in about 100 languages on your own machine.
limit: Careless Whisper study found roughly 1% of transcriptions contained entirely hallucinated phrases; check quotes against the audio.

name: faster-whisper
what: Runs Whisper models several times faster on modest hardware for bulk transcription of footage and recordings.
limit: Same Whisper models, so the same hallucination risk on silence, noise and low-resource languages.

name: WhisperX
what: Adds word-level timestamps and speaker labels to Whisper transcripts, useful for quoting and subtitling video evidence.
limit: README: numbers and symbols cannot be aligned to timings, overlapping speech is handled poorly, diarisation is far from perfect.

name: whisper.cpp
what: Runs Whisper on a laptop CPU or phone with no Python or GPU, for offline field transcription.
limit: Same Whisper models, so the same hallucination risk.

name: pyannote.audio
what: Works out who spoke when in a recording (speaker diarisation), the basis for most open transcription tools.
limit: Models are gated: you must accept user conditions and create a Hugging Face token before first use.

name: AI4Bharat IndicConformer
what: Transcribes speech in the 22 scheduled Indian languages with one open model.
limit: Gated on Hugging Face: you must log in and share contact details to download the files.

name: NVIDIA Parakeet TDT v3
what: Fast open speech-to-text model for European languages with timestamps, an alternative to Whisper for long recordings.
limit: Model card: accuracy varies by language, accent, noise and domain; European languages only, no Indian languages.

name: Omnilingual ASR
what: Open speech recognition for 1,600+ languages, for audio in languages Whisper does not cover.

name: Buzz
what: Desktop app that transcribes and translates audio offline with Whisper, no command line needed.
limit: Same Whisper models, so the same hallucination risk.

name: noScribe
what: Desktop app for interview transcription with speaker identification, built on Whisper and pyannote, fully offline.
limit: Same Whisper models, so the same hallucination risk.

name: aTrain
what: Offline GUI for transcribing interviews with speaker diarisation, aimed at researchers.

name: Good Tape
what: Hosted transcription service built for newsrooms; upload a recording and get a searchable transcript.
limit: Recordings are uploaded to a third-party cloud service; weigh that for sensitive sources.

name: NLLB-200
what: Translates between 200 languages locally, including many low-resource ones commercial tools skip.
limit: Model card: research model, CC-BY-NC, not for legal or medical text, trained on inputs under 512 tokens.

name: IndicTrans2
what: Translates between English and all 22 scheduled Indian languages with an open model you can run offline.

name: Bhashini
what: Government of India language platform offering translation and speech services across Indian languages.
limit: Cloud service run by a government; think before sending sensitive source material.

name: Argos Translate
what: Offline translation library and desktop app; install language packs and translate without any network connection.

name: LibreTranslate
what: Self-hosted translation API and web interface that can run fully offline, a private alternative to cloud translators.

name: OPUS-MT
what: Hundreds of small open translation models for specific language pairs, light enough for a laptop.

name: SeamlessM4T
what: Translates speech and text directly, including speech-to-text translation for foreign-language video.

name: MADLAD-400
what: Apache-licensed translation model covering 400+ languages, usable where NLLB's non-commercial licence is a problem.

name: TranslateGemma
what: Open-weights translation model from Google that also translates text inside images.
limit: Gated: you must accept Google's Gemma licence on Hugging Face before downloading.

name: Firefox Translations
what: Translates web pages inside the browser on your device, so the page text never leaves your machine.

name: AI4Bharat IndicXlit
what: Transliterates names between Roman and 21 Indic scripts, useful for searching name spelling variants.

name: DeepL
what: Commercial machine translation of text and documents in the browser.
limit: Text is uploaded to DeepL's servers.

name: Tesseract
what: Long-standing OCR engine for printed text in 100+ languages; the default for making scans searchable.

name: OCRmyPDF
what: Adds a searchable text layer to scanned PDFs in bulk, using Tesseract underneath.

name: Surya
what: OCR, layout, reading order and table recognition in 90+ languages, strong on complex pages.
limit: Model weights are free only for research, personal use and organisations under $5M funding/revenue.

name: Marker
what: Converts PDFs into clean Markdown or JSON, keeping tables and structure for analysis or LLM use.
limit: Model weights are free only for research, personal use and organisations under $5M funding/revenue.

name: docTR
what: Deep-learning OCR library for detecting and reading text in documents and photos.

name: PaddleOCR
what: OCR and document parsing toolkit covering 100+ languages, turning PDFs and images into structured data.

name: Docling
what: Parses PDFs, Office files and scans into structured text and tables ready for search or LLMs.

name: MinerU
what: Turns complex PDFs and Office documents into Markdown or JSON for search or LLM pipelines.

name: olmOCR
what: Uses a vision language model to linearise difficult PDFs with figures, multi-column layouts and insets.
limit: Needs a recent NVIDIA GPU with at least 12 GB memory; earlier versions hallucinated text on blank pages.

name: Kraken
what: Trainable OCR engine for material standard OCR handles badly, such as historical print and less common scripts.

name: Transkribus
what: Reads handwriting and historical documents with 300+ community-trained models in 100+ languages.
limit: Free tier is 50 credits a month; documents are uploaded to the service.

name: IndicPhotoOCR
what: Reads text in photos (signboards, banners, posters) across 11 Indian languages, useful for geolocation clues.

name: Datashare
what: Self-hosted search engine for large document sets, built by ICIJ for leak investigations; runs on your own machine.

name: OpenAleph
what: Open-source fork of Aleph for storing, searching and cross-referencing large document and entity datasets.
limit: Needs server administration skills to self-host.

name: OCCRP Aleph
what: OCCRP's hosted archive of leaks, company records and sanctions data, searchable by name.
limit: OCCRP now develops Aleph Pro, which is not released as open source; the old open code is unmaintained.

name: Google Pinpoint
what: Google's research tool for journalists to explore and search large collections of documents with AI.
limit: Files sit on Google's servers; generative AI features need an early-access application.

name: NotebookLM (now Gemini Notebook)
what: Ask questions across your uploaded sources and get answers that cite the passages used.
limit: Sources are uploaded to Google's cloud. The old NotebookLM address now redirects to Gemini Notebook.

name: DocumentCloud
what: Platform for uploading, annotating and publishing source documents, run by MuckRock.
limit: Hosted service. The website blocked automated checking (HTTP 403), so the repo was checked instead.

name: AnythingLLM
what: Desktop app to chat with a folder of documents using local models, so files stay on your computer.

name: Open WebUI
what: Self-hosted chat interface for local models with built-in document search (RAG).

name: PrivateGPT
what: Question-answering over your own documents with local models and no data leaving your environment.

name: Kotaemon
what: Open-source interface for chatting with your own documents using local or hosted models.

name: Open Notebook
what: Self-hosted alternative to NotebookLM that works with local or chosen model providers.

name: Ollama
what: Runs open language models on your own computer; the engine behind most local document tools.

name: InVID-WeVerify verification plugin
what: Browser toolkit for verification: keyframes, reverse image search, forensic filters, OCR and synthetic-image checks.
limit: 2026 arXiv study: forensic tools including InVID show high recall but poor specificity; humans outperformed all tools.

name: Content Credentials Verify
what: Checks an image or video for C2PA Content Credentials and shows its signed edit history.
limit: Most files carry no credentials, and platforms often strip them; absence proves nothing.

name: c2patool
what: Command-line reader for C2PA manifests, so provenance checks can run offline.
limit: Absence of a manifest proves nothing about authenticity.

name: SynthID Detector
what: Checks images, video and audio for Google's invisible SynthID watermark.
limit: Only finds SynthID watermarks; content from models without it shows nothing. A negative result is not proof of authenticity.

name: Google Fact Check Explorer
what: Searches published fact-checks by claim to see whether something has already been debunked.

name: Google Lens
what: Reverse image search with visual matching; often the fastest first step in locating or sourcing a picture.
limit: Bellingcat's 2025 test: Lens beat most LLMs at geolocation but lost narrowly to three ChatGPT models.

name: DeepFake-o-Meter
what: Runs a file through many open academic deepfake detectors at once and shows each score.
maintainer: University at Buffalo Media Forensics Lab
limit: Deepfake-Eval-2024: open-source detectors lost about 45-50% AUC on real 2024 deepfakes compared with lab benchmarks.

name: Hive AI-generated content detection
what: Commercial classifier with a free demo that scores images, video and audio as AI-generated or not.
limit: Deepfake-Eval-2024: commercial detectors beat open models but do not reach the accuracy of human forensic analysts.

name: Reality Defender
what: Enterprise deepfake detection for audio, video and images.
limit: Deepfake-Eval-2024: commercial detectors beat open models but do not reach the accuracy of human forensic analysts.

name: ImageWhisperer
what: Image checker for journalists combining AI detection, C2PA, reverse search and fact-check lookups in one report.
limit: Two free checks a day; images are uploaded to the service.

name: ElevenLabs AI Speech Classifier
what: Estimates whether an audio clip was generated with ElevenLabs' own voice tools.
limit: Only covers ElevenLabs audio, and the page says it does not reliably classify Eleven v3 output.

name: Deepfakes Analysis Unit (India)
what: WhatsApp tipline where the public and fact-checkers in India send suspected deepfakes for expert assessment.
limit: Human assessment through a tipline, not an instant automated verdict.

name: TrueMedia (Georgetown)
what: Deepfake detection platform revived at Georgetown University after the original non-profit closed.
limit: Access is by beta request. The original open-sourced models (truemediaorg on GitHub) are unmaintained since early 2025.

name: Bellingcat Auto Archiver
what: Archives social media posts, videos and pages in bulk from a spreadsheet of links.
limit: Not an AI tool; listed because archiving comes before any AI analysis.

name: Deepfake-Eval-2024 (benchmark)
what: Benchmark of real deepfakes from social media in 2024, testing how detectors perform outside the lab.
limit: Finding: detector AUC fell 50% (video), 48% (audio), 45% (image) against earlier academic benchmarks.

name: How Effective Are Publicly Accessible Deepfake Detection Tools?
what: 2026 study comparing six free forensic and AI image-detection tools against professional investigators.
limit: Finding: forensic tools over-flag, AI classifiers under-flag, and human evaluators substantially outperformed every tool.

name: Have LLMs Finally Mastered Geolocation? (Bellingcat)
what: Bellingcat's 500-run test of 20 LLMs on 25 unpublished photos, with Google Lens as the baseline.
limit: Only ChatGPT o3, o4-mini and o4-mini-high beat Google Lens, narrowly; Claude and Mistral lagged well behind.

name: Updated Test of 24 LLMs for Geolocation (Bellingcat via GIJN)
what: Re-run two months later adding GPT-5, Grok 4 and Google AI Mode.
limit: Google AI Mode scored best, but most models hallucinated at some point and even the best confidently named wrong places.

name: Can AI Chatbots Be Used for Geolocation? (Bellingcat, 2023)
what: The 2023 baseline test of Bing AI and Bard, useful for seeing how fast this changed.
limit: Both chatbots struggled and were highly prone to hallucination.

name: ShadowFinder
what: Uses an object's height, shadow length and time to map everywhere on Earth the photo could have been taken.
limit: Needs a reliable time and measurable shadow on flat ground; gives a band of possible locations, not a point.

name: Bellingcat OpenStreetMap Search
what: Finds places where chosen features (e.g. a mosque near a bridge) appear close together in OpenStreetMap.
limit: Not AI; only as complete as OpenStreetMap is for that area.

name: SunCalc
what: Shows sun direction and shadow length for any place and time, the standard chronolocation check.
limit: Not AI; shows sun position only, you still need to measure the shadow yourself.

name: GeoCLIP
what: Open model that predicts GPS coordinates from a single image, run locally.
limit: No independent newsroom test found; treat the predicted coordinates as a lead to verify.

name: StreetCLIP
what: Open CLIP model tuned on street-level imagery to guess country, region or city of a photo.
limit: CC-BY-NC licence, so non-commercial use only; no independent newsroom test found.

name: PIGEON
what: Research code for a CVPR 2024 model trained on street-view data to predict where an image was taken.
limit: Research code with no commits since July 2024; its README links NPR coverage of the privacy concerns.

name: Picarta
what: Upload a photo and get predicted coordinates with confidence scores from an AI model.
limit: Site says accuracy depends on how distinctive the scene is; no independent test found. Photos are uploaded.

name: Doxing via the Lens (paper)
what: Paper showing reasoning models can infer a home address or neighbourhood from ordinary user photos, including selfies.
limit: A privacy warning as much as a capability: the same technique exposes private people.

name: segment-geospatial (SamGeo)
what: Segments buildings, fields, water or damage in satellite imagery with Segment Anything, from a notebook.

name: GeoAI
what: Python package bundling detection, segmentation and change detection for satellite and aerial imagery.

name: Geo-SAM (QGIS plugin)
what: Point-and-click Segment Anything inside QGIS for tracing features in imagery.

name: Clay
what: Open foundation model producing embeddings of satellite imagery, for similarity search and change detection.

name: TorchGeo
what: PyTorch library of geospatial datasets, samplers and pretrained models for training on satellite data.
limit: A developer library; needs ML experience.

name: TerraTorch
what: Toolkit for fine-tuning geospatial foundation models such as Prithvi for floods, burn scars or crops.

name: Prithvi (IBM-NASA)
what: Open Earth-observation foundation models from NASA and IBM for flood, fire-scar and land-use mapping.

name: Google Earth Engine
what: Cloud platform with decades of satellite archives and built-in classifiers for land-change analysis.
limit: Free for academic and research use; commercial use is paid.

name: AlphaEarth Foundations
what: Google's annual satellite embedding dataset in Earth Engine, for similarity search and change mapping without training.
limit: Released as annual embeddings at 10 m squares, so it cannot date a specific event within a year.

name: Dynamic World
what: Near-real-time 10 m global land cover from Sentinel-2, made with deep learning.

name: Earth Index
what: Search satellite imagery by example: mark a mine or feedlot and find similar sites across a region.
limit: Needs an account; results are look-alike candidates to confirm with high-resolution imagery.

name: OlmoEarth
what: Open Earth-observation foundation models and a platform from Allen AI for environmental monitoring.

name: TESSERA
what: Cambridge foundation model giving per-pixel embeddings from Sentinel-1/2 time series for land classification.

name: Open-CD
what: Toolbox of change-detection models for comparing before and after satellite images.

name: SkyTruth Cerulean
what: Detects oil slicks in Sentinel-1 radar with ML and links them to likely source vessels.
limit: Detections come with confidence scores; treat a slick or source match as a lead.

name: Global Fishing Watch map
what: Maps fishing activity and vessels worldwide using ML on AIS and satellite radar detections.

name: spaCy
what: Fast NLP library for pulling names, organisations and places out of large text collections.

name: GLiNER
what: Extracts any entity type you name (e.g. vessel, shell company) without training a model.

name: Stanza
what: Stanford NLP toolkit for tokenising, parsing and NER in many languages.

name: AI4Bharat IndicNER
what: Named-entity recognition for 11 Indian languages.
limit: Gated on Hugging Face: you must log in and share contact details to download.

name: LangExtract
what: Uses an LLM to extract structured facts from long text and links each one to its source span.
limit: README: accuracy of inferred information depends on the chosen LLM and prompt; check highlighted spans.

name: BERTopic
what: Groups thousands of posts or documents into readable topics using embeddings.

name: Splink
what: Probabilistic record linkage: matches people or companies across datasets without shared IDs.

name: nomenklatura
what: Entity resolution and deduplication toolkit for FollowTheMoney data, with a human review loop.

name: FollowTheMoney
what: Shared data model for people, companies, assets and relationships used by OpenSanctions and OpenAleph.

name: OpenSanctions and yente
what: Open database of sanctions and politically exposed persons, with a self-hosted matching API.
limit: Commercial use needs a paid data licence; a name match is a lead, not an identification.

name: OpenRefine
what: Cleans messy spreadsheets, clusters name variants and reconciles them against external databases.

name: Gephi
what: Desktop network analysis and visualisation for mapping accounts, companies or citations.

name: GraphRAG
what: Builds a knowledge graph from documents with an LLM, then answers questions across the whole set.

name: OpenOSINT
what: Agent and MCP server with 21 public-source tools (DNS, RDAP, WHOIS, GDELT, dorks). 1,939 stars.
limit: Passive tools work keyless; Shodan, Censys, VirusTotal and breach checks need keys. Infrastructure focus.

name: mcp-shodan
what: MCP server for Shodan host search, DNS and CVE lookups. 191 stars.
limit: Needs your own Shodan API key.

name: osint-mcp-server (badchars)
what: 37 tools over 12 sources: DNS, WHOIS, crt.sh, BGP, Wayback, plus Shodan and VirusTotal. 62 stars.
limit: 21 tools work without keys; the other 16 need paid or registered API keys.

name: mcp-wayback-machine
what: MCP server and CLI to check, fetch and save Wayback Machine snapshots. 66 stars.

name: gdelt-mcp-server
what: Searches GDELT global news coverage and US TV transcripts from an agent; no API key. 10 stars.

name: World Intel MCP
what: 160 tools over free public APIs: conflict events, aircraft, maritime warnings, sanctions, markets. 1,079 stars.
limit: Some tools need API keys; README flags which.

name: OpenRegistry
what: Hosted MCP for live company records from 27 official national registries. 23 stars.
limit: Hosted service with sign-in; its README does not mention India.

name: Sanctions Screening MCP
what: Screens names against OFAC, EU, UK and UN lists offline from a local mirror; no key. 4 stars.
limit: Fuzzy name matches are leads, not identifications.

name: Sift
what: MCP server and skills cross-referencing OpenSanctions, ICIJ Offshore Leaks, Companies House, SEC EDGAR and CourtListener. 6 stars.
limit: Small project; US and UK sources dominate.

name: osmmcp
what: OpenStreetMap MCP server: geocoding, nearby places and routing for an agent. 32 stars.

name: MoSPI eSankhyiki MCP (India)
what: Official Indian statistics ministry MCP server for economic, demographic and social indicators. 148 stars.
limit: Statistics only; no company, court, land or tender records.

name: data.gov.in MCP server
what: Exposes India's open government data portal APIs to agents. 2 stars.
limit: Needs a data.gov.in API key; no commits since November 2025.

name: mcp-india-tenders
what: Searches Indian government tenders from CPPP, eProc Rajasthan and defence portals. 2 stars.
limit: Tiny project with no commits since December 2025.

name: Awesome OSINT MCP Servers
what: Curated directory of about 115 OSINT MCP servers by category. 548 stars.
limit: Includes people-search and breach-data servers; listings are not vetted for accuracy or ethics.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: claude-skills-journalism
what: Skill packs for newsrooms: source verification, C2PA, web archiving, FOIA requests, data journalism. 453 stars.
limit: Public-records skills are US-centric (FOIA, New Jersey OPRA) plus Brazil's LAI.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: osint-investigation skill
what: Berkeley Protocol-aligned skill for geolocation, photo verification and account checks that outputs a lead sheet. 7 stars.
limit: Methodology only, no bundled tools; public-records references cover Brazil.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: Investigators Co-Pilot
what: Claude Code plugin for case management with evidence capture, A-F source grading and 54 lookup adapters. 76 stars.
limit: Needs a paid Claude plan; some adapters need outside paid keys. Includes username and email lookups.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: OSINT Forge Skills
what: 16 skills with offline Python helpers for evidence preservation, competing hypotheses and cited reports. 10 stars.
limit: Analyses files you supply; does not fetch archives or registries itself. French sources (BODACC) featured.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: geo-sleuth
what: Agent skill that geolocates a photo using OpenStreetMap geometry, skylines, satellite imagery and street view. 7,088 stars.
limit: README admits no blind-test accuracy figure yet; published examples are regression checks on already-solved photos.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: bullshit-detector
what: Agent skills that break a video, article or post into claims and check each against sources. 163 stars.
limit: Verdicts come from an LLM's web search; Full Fact logged dozens of chatbot fact-check errors in 2026.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: agentic-newsroom
what: Data-journalism skills that load raw records into SQLite, screen for leads and track findings. 1 star.
limit: A contest entry built around US lobbying data, not a general tool.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: Newsroom extension
what: 18 skills for Claude and Gemini CLI covering FOIA, corporate research, evidence preservation and libel review. 8 stars.
limit: Includes subject-dossier skills; legal content is US-oriented and is not legal advice.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: Anthropic Agent Skills
what: Official examples and specification for SKILL.md packs, the starting point for writing your own.
limit: Not OSINT-specific.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: GPT Researcher
what: Autonomous agent that searches the web and writes a cited research report on a question.
limit: Tow Center found AI search tools gave wrong answers to over 60% of news-citation queries; check every source.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: Taranis AI
what: Self-hosted OSINT monitoring: collects news sources, then uses NLP to cluster, summarise and tag items.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: STORM
what: Stanford system that researches a topic and drafts a long, cited background article.
limit: No commits since September 2025.

category: Agent skills, prompts and agent frameworks for investigations
name: Journalist's Toolbox AI
what: Regularly updated directory of AI tools, prompts and guides for reporters.
limit: A directory, not a tested evaluation.

name: Why AI Models Are Bad at Verifying Photos (Tow Center)
what: Test of seven chatbots asked to identify the location, date and photographer of ten news photos.
maintainer: Tow Center for Digital Journalism / CJR
limit: Only 14 of 280 answers got location, date and source right.

name: AI Search Has a Citation Problem (Tow Center)
what: Test of eight AI search tools asked to identify the source article of news quotes.
maintainer: Tow Center for Digital Journalism / CJR
limit: Over 60% of answers were wrong; Perplexity erred 37% of the time, Grok 3 94%.

name: What Journalists Should Know About Deepfake Detection in 2025 (Tow Center)
what: Plain-language guide to how detectors work and why they fail on real-world media.
maintainer: Tow Center for Digital Journalism / CJR
limit: Cites an experiment where journalists over-relied on detector output when it matched their instinct.

name: Spotting the deepfakes in this year of elections (Reuters Institute / WITNESS)
what: WITNESS researchers tested public AI detectors and explain where they break.
maintainer: Reuters Institute; shirin anlen and Raquel Vázquez Llorente
limit: Lowering resolution or cropping a known deepfake flipped a detector's verdict to 'not a deepfake'.

name: TRIED Benchmark (WITNESS)
what: Framework for judging AI detection tools on real-world usefulness, built from WITNESS casework.
limit: A framework, not a league table of tools.

name: Careless Whisper: Speech-to-Text Hallucination Harms
what: Study measuring how often Whisper invents text that was never spoken.
limit: About 1% of transcriptions had hallucinated phrases; 38% of those included explicit harms.

name: Full Fact: AI chatbots and misinformation trial
what: UK fact-checker's 2026 log of what major chatbots said about false claims it was checking.
limit: 39 major errors and 67 incorrect responses in five months, including calling AI-generated images real.

name: News Integrity in AI Assistants (EBU / BBC)
what: Study by 22 public broadcasters in 14 languages on how AI assistants answer news questions.
limit: Reported 45% of answers had at least one significant issue (figure from EBU press coverage).

name: Poynter AI ethics starter kit (2025 update)
what: Template newsroom AI policy, updated with sections on visual journalism and AI products.

name: AP standards around generative AI
what: The Associated Press's published rules on how its journalists may and may not use generative AI.

name: BBC guidance: the use of artificial intelligence
what: BBC editorial guidance on AI use, transparency and human oversight.

name: Paris Charter on AI and Journalism
what: Ten principles on AI in journalism drafted by RSF and 16 partner organisations.

name: PAI Responsible Practices for Synthetic Media
what: Framework on disclosure and labelling of synthetic media, with case studies from signatories.

name: Reporter's Guide to Detecting AI-Generated Content (GIJN)
what: GIJN's practical guide to spotting AI-made images, video and audio by inspection and tools.
limit: Visual tells go out of date quickly as generators improve.

name: How newsrooms are using AI in investigations (Nieman Lab, Oct 2026)
what: Round-up of how investigative teams actually use agents and LLMs, with their stated limits.
limit: Quoted finding: AI is good at generating leads, much less capable of establishing publishable evidence.
